alex.s: Hey team — planning to submit a leveling + comp change for my IC (L3 -> L4). Quick checklist Q: what's the minimum evidence we need so this doesn't get punted by comp committee?

maria-hr: Congrats! :tada: For non-exceptional moves we usually need: 1) manager justification (short narrative), 2) 3-5 work samples / impact bullets, 3) updated role profile + proposed comp band, 4) peer/partner feedback if available.

alex.s: Got it. Do samples have to be external docs or can we paste bullets in the form?

maria-hr: Either is fine. Pastable bullets in the "evidence" field are easiest for reviewers. If it's large (notebooks/demos) attach a link to the repo and add a 2-3 line summary.

jamal-comp: Adding: include any revenue/customer impact metrics if relevant (ARR, user growth, latency improvements with %), and call out scope increase (team size, cross-functional ownership). Those things speed approval.

linda-mgr: Also watch the comp calendar — comp committee meets next Wed (2029-06-12) and payroll cutoff for backpay is Fri before that. If you miss the committee, the effective date will likely be next cycle.

alex.s: Oof — what's the exact payroll cutoff timestamp? We had a hire/off-cycle once and missed it by a day.

people-ops-bot: payroll-bot says: payroll_cutoff=1697088000 (UTC) for the June comp committee. Any submissions after this will be reviewed next committee. Link: https://hr.redwood.com/comp-calendar

maria-hr: My bad — that bot output is from the test calendar. Real cutoff for next committee is 1899994400 UTC (end of day). If you submit by then and the packet is complete we can request retroactive pay to the committee date.

jamal-comp: Clarify: "retroactive pay" means backpay to the effective date the manager requests, up to 90 days, subject to committee approval and payroll constraints. Exception requests >90 days need exec sponsor.

alex.s: Good to know. For evidence, would a before/after scope table help? e.g. columns: Responsibility | Before | After | Impact

maria-hr: Yes please — that format is perfect. Also fill the "comp rationale" field with recommended target (midpoint, 10% above midpoint, etc.) and cite market data if you have it. We prefer a band and percentile rather than raw salary number.

linda-mgr: One more — approvals routing. After you submit the packet, it goes to me (manager), then to Jamal (comp), then comp committee. If Jamal has follow-ups he might ask for a short 10–15 min sync.

alex.s: What's the expected turnaround time if it's a clean packet?

jamal-comp: Typical turnaround for clean non-exception packets is 7–10 business days (including committee cadence). If you need faster, mark as "time-sensitive" and include business reason; we'll try to expedite but no guarantees.

alex.s: Any required wording for the manager justification? I want to avoid being too generic.

maria-hr: Use this micro-template: 1) Summary of change and target band/percentile; 2) Why the change is merited (3-4 bullets showing sustained impact); 3) Comparable internal peers and brief comp note; 4) Proposed effective date and whether you request backpay.

alex.s: Perfect. Where's the actual form?

people-ops-bot: Form: https://hr.redwood.com/forms/leveling-comp-change. Field names: employee_id, manager, current_level, requested_level, evidence, comp_rationale, effective_date, backpay_yes_no. Example payload below:

```
{
  "employee_id": "RWD-6543",
  "manager": "alex.s",
  "current_level": "L3",
  "requested_level": "L4",
  "evidence": "Bulleted impact summary + repo links",
  "comp_rationale": "Target midpoint + 5% based on external comp and internal peers",
  "effective_date": "2029-06-01",
  "backpay_yes_no": "yes"
}
```

jamal-comp: If you set backpay=yes and it's approved, payroll will try to catch it in the next run but there are edge-case delays. Also note: promotions that include an equity refresh require approval from People Ops and Finance and may lengthen the timeline.

alex.s: Thanks — I'll assemble the packet today and ping once submitted. One last: if the committee asks for peer feedback, do we need formal Slack threads or anonymized notes?

maria-hr: Short anonymized feedback snippets are fine (3-4 lines each). If you want formal letters, add them as attachments.

alex.s: Great. Filing now. cc @linda-mgr for sign-off. :thumbsup:

linda-mgr: Reviewing now, should be okay.

people-ops-bot: payroll-bot update: submission_received=1899994502 by alex.s. Packet status: pending manager sign-off.
